Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.dhKEM.headline: Cslib.Crypto.DecodablePrimeOrderGroupFamily.GapCDH.dhKEMROMINDCCA
Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.dhKEM.why: typed DH-KEM CCA-to-gap-CDH reduction; the equality says that for every decodable prime-order group family `F`, key length `keyLen`, parameter `n`, group `d`, exponents `a, b : ZMod (F.order d)`, and coin-tape machine replaying `adversary` at `n`, running `dhKEMToGapCDHWord` on the encoded challenge `(n, d, encode d (a • g), encode d (b • g))` against `ddhWordOracle d b` has the exact `PMF` law of drawing saved coins from `uniformList (dhKEMCoinBudget …)` and encoding `runDDH d b` of this reduction on `savedCoinDHKEMAdversary … coins` with uniform `keyLen n`-bit keys (`gapCDHWordGame_dhKEMToGapCDHWord_eq` lifts it to the full search game); the Gap-CDH game has one world and runs the word reduction only on such encoded challenges

Cslib.Crypto.cbcReduction.why: tracked in #4894 and #5293 section 2 (Public-key encryption: finite CTR, OFB and CBC reductions bound queries, not time; the uniform `BlockCipher.cbcToPrpDistinguisher` is certified)

Cslib.Crypto.ctrReduction.why: tracked in #5293 section 2 (Public-key encryption: finite CTR and OFB reductions bound queries, not time; the uniform `ctrToPrfDistinguisher` and `ofbToPrfDistinguisher` are certified)

Cslib.Crypto.KEM.hybridCipherAdversary.headline: Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa
Cslib.Crypto.KEM.hybridCipherAdversary.why: typed KEM/DEM hybrid cipher adversary; the equality says that for each challenge bit the word adversary's one-time DEM game has the law of the typed one-time experiment of this adversary of `wordKEM` and `adversary.toHybridTwoStage n`, with keys from `sampleList (keyLen n)` and every message pair valid

Cslib.Crypto.KEM.hybridDistinguisher.headline: Cslib.Crypto.Encryption.KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa
Cslib.Crypto.KEM.hybridDistinguisher.why: typed KEM/DEM hybrid distinguisher; the equality says that for each challenge bit and every framed challenge `encKEMChallenge (pk, (key, ct))`, the only inputs the KEM games give it, the word distinguisher has the law of this distinguisher of `wordCipher` and `adversary.toHybridTwoStage n` on `(pk, ct, key)`

Cslib.Crypto.KEM.hybridHiddenBitDistingu.why: not an asymptotic reduction: the single hidden-bit KEM distinguisher of the exact bound `KEM.advantage_hybrid_le_two_mul` (Exercise 11.9(b)); every referring theorem is concrete and none applies an assumption; its certified word twin `Encryption.hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher` (`isPPT_hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher`, equal law by `eval_hybridToKEMHiddenBitDistinguisher_encKEMChallenge`) has only concrete referrers too; the asymptotic headline `Encryption.KEMINDCPA.hybrid_indcpa` applies KEM security to the per-bit `hybridToKEMDistinguisher` instead, and a hidden-bit headline would restate it

Cslib.Crypto.ofbReduction.why: tracked in #5293 section 2 (Public-key encryption: finite CTR and OFB reductions bound queries, not time; the uniform `ctrToPrfDistinguisher` and `ofbToPrfDistinguisher` are certified)

Cslib.Crypto.Forger.toTyped.why: not a reduction: the typed view of a word forger (an adapter), on the bounding side only of the exact identities `SignatureScheme.succProbability_eufCmaGame` and `succProbability_eufOneTimeGame` (word game = typed experiment of `S.toScheme n` against `A.toTyped n`); every referring theorem is concrete, and its referring definitions `TreeSignature.treeGame`, `treeGameWith`, and `MACScheme.toForgeExperiment` are experiments that the tree-signature and MAC theorems bound; assumptions are applied only to word-level reductions (`TreeSignature.eufCMA_scheme_of_prf_of_inv` applies them to `indexedForger` and `treeCoinAdversary`, neither of which mentions it), never to a program built from `A.toTyped n`

Cslib.Crypto.SecureSketch.jointSketch.why: not a reduction: the joint law of a source and its sketch

Cslib.Crypto.FuzzyExtractor.lweFuzzyExtr.why: not a reduction: the Construction 4.1 fuzzy extractor of a decoder, the scheme on the bounding side of the common-matrix identity

Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.publicKe.why: not a reduction: a hybrid game of the key chain, applied to no adversary

Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Leveled.exactLe.why: #5293: no general strict-PPT witness is established here: it draws its hop selector exactly uniformly from `Fin 3` and the link and bit indices from `Fin (depth n)` and `Fin (capacity n)`, laws that a clocked fair-coin machine (`IsPPTOn`), whose output probabilities are dyadic, does not produce in general (an instance whose output law ignores the draws may still have a witness); the certified `modLeveledAdversary` is linked to it only by the bound `advantage_exactLeveledAdversary_modLeveledAdversary_le`; every referring theorem is concrete, but the asymptotic headline `Leveled.indCPA_scheme` uses neither it nor `modLeveledAdversary` (it goes through the dyadic `linkAdversary` and `zeroLinkAdversary`), so it stays a gap

Cslib.Crypto.Homomorphic.Scheme.exactLin.why: #5293: no general strict-PPT witness is established here: it draws the link and bit indices exactly uniformly from `Fin (depth n)` and `Fin (capacity n)`, laws that a clocked fair-coin machine (`IsPPTOn`), whose output probabilities are dyadic, does not produce in general (it does when both are powers of two; an instance whose output law ignores the draws may still have a witness); the certified `modLinkAdversary` is linked to it only by the bound `advantage_exactLinkAdversary_modLinkAdversary_le`; every referring theorem is concrete, but the asymptotic headline `Leveled.indCPA_scheme` uses neither it nor `modLinkAdversary` (it goes through `Scheme.negligible_publicKeyChainHybrid`, the dyadic `linkAdversary`), so it stays a gap

Cslib.Crypto.KeyDerivation.listGuessToGu.why: information-theoretic: list-to-singleton index-sampling step of listGuessAdvantage_le_mul_guessAdvantage for arbitrary list guessers; no computational assumption is applied to it

Cslib.Crypto.KeyDerivation.roToGuess.why: information-theoretic: Theorem 8.10 for all guessers; the wrapper samples the whole oracle table and no computational assumption is applied to it

Cslib.Crypto.KeyDerivation.roToListGuess.why: information-theoretic: Theorem 8.10 for all guessers; the wrapper samples the whole oracle table and no computational assumption is applied to it

Cslib.Crypto.Regev.lorDistinguisher.headline: Cslib.Crypto.Regev.lorIndCPA_of_decisionLWE
Cslib.Crypto.Regev.lorDistinguisher.why: typed per-bit Regev left-or-right distinguisher; the equality says that at every security parameter and on the canonical word of every public matrix `A`, the hidden-bit word distinguisher draws a fair bit `b` and outputs `g ^^ b`, where `g` is the guess of this distinguisher at `b` on `A` with `Q security` queries and the typed view `typedLoRAdversary adversary security`; it holds at every `A`, so under both the real and the uniform `DecisionLWE` ensembles

Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.naorR.why: #5293 baseline lane: typed PMF distinguisher of the exact per-instance bound `advantage_naorReingold_le_sum`, which holds for arbitrary typed adversaries at one group; the certified word-level headline `DDH.negligible_naorReingoldProbGame` uses a different reduction (`naorReingoldToDDHDistinguisher`), with no equality between them

#5293 baseline lane: typed PMF distinguisher of the exact per-instance bound `advantage_naorReingold_le_sum`, which holds for arbitrary typed adversaries at one group; the certified word-level headline `DDH.negligible_naorReingoldProbGame` uses a different reduction (`naorReingoldToDDHDistinguisher`), with no equality between them

Cslib.Crypto.paillierToDCR.headline: Cslib.Crypto.Paillier.DCR.indcpaOn_paillier
Cslib.Crypto.paillierToDCR.why: typed fixed-modulus Paillier CPA-to-DCR reduction; the private equality says that for every word adversary, bit `b`, parameter `n`, modulus `N` and unit `y` modulo `N ^ 2`, the word distinguisher `dcrDistinguisher adversary b n` on `(N, y.val)` is, as a program, `paillierToDCR N (typedAdversary adversary n N) b y`; the private typed view runs `adversary.restrict validMessages` on `encNat N`, reads the chosen messages modulo `N` and gives the challenge as `encNat` of its least representative modulo `N ^ 2`; the typed reduction admits every pair of `ZMod N`, and the view answers an inadmissible word pair (`m₀ ≥ N` or `m₁ ≥ N`) with `false`, as the word distinguisher does; both DCR games run the word distinguisher only on such inputs (`y = s ^ N` or a uniform unit), so the equation covers both worlds; the headline's random-world step is derived from it

Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.peder.headline: Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.DiscreteLog.pedersenScheme_binding_pedersenKeyDistProb
Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.peder.why: typed Pedersen binding-to-discrete-logarithm reduction; the equality says that for every group `d`, key `h`, parameter `n` and binding adversary, the word reduction on the encoded key `(d, encode d h)` is, as a program, this reduction on the adversary read through `pedersenCollisionOf` (the reading of `pedersenBindingGame_eq`) with its exponent output as the binary word of its value; the discrete-logarithm game is a search game with one world and runs the word reduction only on such keys, `h = α • g`

Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.schno.why: tracked in #5293 section 2 (Signatures and MACs: Schnorr and Fiat–Shamir forking reductions)

Cslib.Crypto.SignatureScheme.toScheme.why: not a reduction: the typed scheme of a word-level signature scheme

Cslib.Crypto.Experiment.guessBit.why: not a reduction: the hidden-bit form of a pair of experiments

Cslib.Crypto.plantInverter.why: not an asymptotic reduction: the exactly uniform guess of (13.6) (Lemma 13.5) on the typed game, for every typed adversary; a strict-PPT sampler draws that index exactly only when t is a power of two, so it has no efficiency certificate; `Cslib.Crypto.repeatedInverter` (dyadic guess, running `slotInverter`) is the certified word-level reduction in `OneWay/Repeated.lean`

Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.prvSimToPrv1.why: adversary conversion between garbling notions (BHR12 relations) over per-instance games; not listed in #5293 section 2; recorded when this check was introduced

Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.BMR16.reduction.why: per-instance BMR16 garbling reduction; a family theorem (#6068) would rest on a novel asymptotic mixed-modulus CCR assumption and needs mixed-modulus circuit encodings, residue inputs and side information hiding the projection tables; out of #5293 B4 (decision 5)

Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.BinaryToOneHot.red.why: per-instance reduction for the one-hot gadget, which is not a garbling scheme for functions and hashes all `2 ^ (n + 1)` label positions; a family statement needs a `logrow` garbling scheme; out of #5293 B4 (decision 5)

Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.FreeXOR.reduction.headline: Cslib.Crypto.CircularCorrelationRobust.negligible_prvSimAdvantage_freeXOR
Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.FreeXOR.reduction.why: per-instance hybrid step of free-XOR privacy; the equality says that against every fixed full-label oracle `O` the word reduction's output law at parameter `k` is `B`'s choice of `(f, x)` followed, when `x` has `f.n` bits and `8 q ≤ 2 ^ k`, by this step on `toCircuit f` with the key-only hash `fun key t => CCR.atLevel hash k (key, false) t`, the tweaks `slotTweak`, queries lifted via `CCR.keyOnlyEmbed`, and `B`'s guess on the words of the view and, otherwise, by `B`'s guess on `⊥`; `CCR.advantage_keyOnly` transfers key-only CCR to full-label CCR and both CCR worlds first draw a fixed oracle, so it covers both; `prvSim_freeXOR` repackages the headline (#5293 B4)

Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.HalfGates.reductio.headline: Cslib.Crypto.CircularCorrelationRobust.negligible_prvSimAdvantage_simWord
Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.HalfGates.reductio.why: per-instance hybrid step of half-gates privacy; the private equality says that against every fixed oracle `O` the word reduction's output law at parameter `k` is `B`'s choice of `(f, x)` followed, when `x` has `f.n` bits and `2 q ≤ 2 ^ k`, by this step on `toCircuit f` with the hash `CCR.atLevel hash k`, the tweaks `slotTweak` and `B`'s guess on the words of the view and, otherwise, by `B`'s guess on `⊥`; both CCR worlds first draw a fixed oracle (the circular oracle at a uniform offset, or a uniform function), so it covers both; `prvSim_halfGates` repackages the headline (#5293 B4, decision 6)

Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.reduction.headline: Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.negligible_prvSimAdvantage_simWord
Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.reduction.why: per-instance hybrid step of point-and-permute privacy; the equality says that against every label table the word reduction's output law is `B`'s choice of `(f, x)` followed, when `x` has `f.n` bits, by this step on `toCircuit f` at a uniform index below `dyadicSize (P k)` and, otherwise, by `B`'s guess on `⊥`; `prvSim_pointPermute` repackages the headline (#5293 B4, decision 6)

Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.RerandomizableGarb.why: per-instance rerandomization-privacy distinguisher; not listed in #5293 section 2; recorded when this check was introduced
per-instance rerandomization-privacy distinguisher; not listed in #5293 section 2; recorded when this check was introduced
per-instance rerandomization-privacy distinguisher; not listed in #5293 section 2; recorded when this check was introduced

Cslib.Crypto.Garbling.Switch.reduction.why: per-instance switch-system reduction; a family statement needs a notion whose simulator receives the input-dependent control bits, and a novel asymptotic form of `CCR.Arithmetic`; out of #5293 B4 (decision 5)

Cslib.Crypto.PRF.hashReduction.why: finite PRF reduction `B_F` of Boneh–Shoup Theorem 7.7 with a query bound only (`isQueryBounded_hashReduction`); the asymptotic Theorem 7.7, which needs its efficiency witness, stays open on #5790

Cslib.Crypto.PRF.idealQueries.why: information-theoretic: the multi-query UHF adversary `B'_H` is bounded only through the statistical `ε`-UHF bound `UHF.eval_multiQueryExperiment_le`, which holds for all adversaries; no computational assumption is applied to it

Cslib.Crypto.PRF.multiKeyReduction.headline: Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.multiKey_constantCount
Cslib.Crypto.PRF.multiKeyReduction.why: finite multi-key PRF hybrid reduction; the equality says that for a length-preserving family, every `t`, `j`, `n` and adversary, and every table `T` on `n`-bit strings, the law of the word reduction `prfMultiReduction family t j adversary` on `adversary n []` against the word oracle `randomFunctionOracle n T` is the law of this reduction for `PRF.atLevel family n` on `(OracleCodec.withOp (Fin t) (OracleCodec.bitString n)).adapt (adversary n [])` against `T`; the ideal PRF game runs the word reduction against a uniform `T` and the real game against `T = PRF.atLevel family n key` for a uniform key (its word oracle `prfOracle family n key`), so the equation covers both worlds

Cslib.Crypto.PRG.nextBitPredictor.why: tracked in #5293 section 2 (Symmetric: finite next-bit predictor with abstract admissibility)

Cslib.Crypto.PRG.Generator.parallelReduc.why: not an asymptotic reduction: finite-type PRG hybrid kernel of Theorem 3.2 (the identity holds for every kernel and no theorem applies a security assumption to it); `Cslib.Crypto.sequenceTest` (via `ComputationallyIndistinguishable.replicate_bind`) is the certified word-level reduction in `PseudorandomGenerator/Parallel.lean`

Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.targetForger.why: generic typed target-forgery reduction (`#7068`): both current word-level headlines certify and apply it via explicit word reductions (`targetForgerWord` / `isOraclePPTOn_targetForgerWord` / `eval_eufCmaGame_targetForgerWord_eq` in `Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.negligible_extractedTokenWordGame`, and `targetForgerWordOf creditNoteDecoder` / `isOraclePPTOn_targetForgerWordOf` / `Conservation.eval_eufCmaGame_noteForgerWord_eq` in `Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.Conservation.negligible_extractedConservationWordGame`), and no third headline uses it; stays a `gap` under `check_reduction_witnesses.py` because the equalities cover `WordSignatureScheme` word instances rather than arbitrary `(PK, SK, Message, Opening, Target, Sig)` types, and `scope: "instance"` allows only one non-concrete headline per entry

Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.Conservation.headline: Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.Conservation.negligible_extractedConservationWordGame
Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.Conservation.why: extracted VOLE-ACT commitment-binding reduction; the certified word program `commitmentBindingReductionWord` is uniform strict PPT (`isPPTOn_commitmentBindingReductionWord`); the equality is instance-scoped: it holds at bit-string protocol types for every `WordSignatureScheme` `S`, supported signature length bound `sigBound`, `com`, injective `tag`, adversary `A`, `n`, `ck`, and key `k`, equating `commitmentBindingReductionWord sigBound com tag S A n ck` in `PMF` law with `Conservation.commitmentBindingReduction (com n ck) (pairScheme S tag n) (A.toTyped n ck) k`; the headline instantiates `com := wordNoteCom H` and `tag := wordTag`, proves `noteCollisionFinder` uniform strict PPT (`isPPT_noteCollisionFinder`), and applies `CollisionResistant H` via `eval_commitmentBindingReductionWord_eq`

Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.Conservation.headline: Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.Conservation.negligible_extractedConservationWordGame
Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.Conservation.why: extracted VOLE-ACT note-forgery reduction; the certified word program `noteForgerWord` is uniform strict oracle PPT (`isOraclePPTOn_noteForgerWord`); the equality is instance-scoped: it holds at bit-string protocol types for every `WordSignatureScheme` `S`, supported signature length bound `sigBound`, `com`, injective `tag`, adversary `A`, `n`, and `ck`, equating `S.eufCmaGame` running `targetForgerWordOf creditNoteDecoder sigBound (noteTarget com tag)` around `noteForgerWord sigBound com tag S A` in `PMF` law with `(pairScheme S tag n).eufCmaExperiment` running `targetForger (Credit.target (com n ck) Prod.mk)` around `Conservation.noteForger (com n ck) Prod.mk (pairScheme S tag n) (A.toTyped n ck)` (proved via `eval_runExtracted_noteForgerWord_eq`); the headline instantiates `com := wordNoteCom H` and `tag := wordTag`, proves `sampledConservationForger` oracle PPT (`isOraclePPT_sampledConservationForger`), and applies `S.EUFCMA`

Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.reduceRedemp.headline: Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.negligible_extractedRedemptionWordGame_of_wordOneMoreUnforgeable
Cslib.Crypto.AnonymousToken.reduceRedemp.why: extracted single-issuer random-target prefix-and-slot reduction (`#7068`); the certified word program `reduceRedemptionsWord` is uniform strict oracle PPT (`isOraclePPT_reduceRedemptionsWord`); the equality is instance-scoped: it holds at word signature instances for every `WordSignatureScheme` `S`, `N`, `targets`, `budget`, `slotWord`, `n`, `Message`, `encM`, total decoder `dec : Decoder encM`, injective `slot : Message ↪ Fin (N n)` satisfying `∀ w, slotWord n w = (slot (dec.decode w)).val`, and `WordRedemptionAdversary` `A`, equating `oneMoreWordGame S N targets budget (reduceRedemptionsWord budget slotWord A) n` in `PMF` law with `Signature.oneMoreExperiment (S.toScheme n) (targets n) (budget n) (reduceRedemptions slot (budget n) (A.toTyped dec (N n) n))`; the headline requires `WordOneMoreUnforgeable S N targets budget`, polynomial-time `budget + 1` and `slotWord`, and `IsOraclePPT (encRedemptionTokenList encBits) A`, certifying `reduceRedemptionsWord` via `isOraclePPT_reduceRedemptionsWord` and transferring the finite bound through `extractedRedemptionWordGame_succProbability_le` and `eval_oneMoreWordGame_reduceRedemptionsWord_eq`

Cslib.Crypto.LubyRackoff.feistel3Reducti.headline: Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.prp_lubyRackoffCipher
Cslib.Crypto.LubyRackoff.feistel3Reducti.why: three-round Luby–Rackoff hybrid reduction; the certified program is `prfMultiReduction family 3 j (lubyRackoffAdversary adversary)`, oracle PPT by `isOraclePPT_prfMultiReduction` from the adapter's certificate; the equality says that for a length-preserving family, every `j` and `n`, and every table `T` on `n`-bit strings, its law on `adversary n []` against the word oracle `randomFunctionOracle n T` is the law of this reduction for `PRF.atLevel family n` on `(pairCodec n).adapt (adversary n [])` against `T`; both PRF games run it against such a table (a uniform `T` in the ideal game, `PRF.atLevel family n key` for a uniform key in the real game), so the equation covers both worlds

Cslib.Crypto.LubyRackoff.feistel4StrongR.headline: Cslib.Crypto.PseudorandomFunction.strongPRP_lubyRackoff4Cipher
Cslib.Crypto.LubyRackoff.feistel4StrongR.why: four-round strong Luby–Rackoff hybrid reduction; the certified program is `prfMultiReduction family 4 j (strongLubyRackoffAdversary adversary)`, oracle PPT by `isOraclePPT_prfMultiReduction` from the adapter's certificate; the equality says that for a length-preserving family, every `j` and `n`, and every table `T` on `n`-bit strings, its law on `adversary n []` against the word oracle `randomFunctionOracle n T` is the law of this reduction for `PRF.atLevel family n` on `(strongPermCodec n).adapt (adversary n [])` against `T`; both PRF games run it against such a table (a uniform `T` in the ideal game, `PRF.atLevel family n key` for a uniform key in the real game), so the equation covers both worlds

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.FujisakiOkamoto.S.headline: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.FujisakiOkamoto.WordPKE.INDCPA.romINDCCABot
Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.FujisakiOkamoto.S.why: typed IND-CPA reduction of FO^⊥; the private equality says that for each challenge bit and parameter `n` the IND-CPA game of `P` against the word reduction for `A` has the law of the typed IND-CPA experiment of `finitePKE n` against this reduction of `finiteScheme n` for the saved-coin typed view `savedCoinAdversary … n`, when the ciphertexts of `P` fit (`CiphertextFits`, a premise of the headline) and the coin-tape machine replays `A` on the challenge words at `n`, as such a machine does for every uniform strict oracle-PPT `A` of an efficient family with polynomial-time key length; under `CiphertextFits` the word filter `simBotCheck (toExplicitCoin n)` agrees with the typed filter `simBotCheck (finitePKE n)` on represented caches; `IsEfficient.exists_typedAdversary` restates it as an equality of advantages under `∃`

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.FujisakiOkamoto.S.headline: Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.FujisakiOkamoto.WordPKE.INDCPA.romINDCCA
Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.FujisakiOkamoto.S.why: typed IND-CPA reduction of FO-notbot; the private equality says that for each challenge bit and parameter `n` the IND-CPA game of `P` against the word reduction for `A` has the law of the typed IND-CPA experiment of `finitePKE n` against this reduction of `finiteScheme n` for the saved-coin typed view `savedCoinAdversary … n`, when the ciphertexts of `P` fit (`CiphertextFits`, a premise of the headline) and the coin-tape machine replays `A` on the challenge words at `n`, as such a machine does for every uniform strict oracle-PPT `A` of an efficient family with polynomial-time key length; `IsEfficient.exists_typedAdversary` restates it as an equality of advantages under `∃`

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.MPC.Protocol.real.why: not a reduction: the real joint view-and-output distribution of a protocol execution (`semiHonestAdvantage_compose_le` states the world-replacement gap with it)

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.MPC.idealJoint.why: not a reduction: the ideal joint view-and-output sampler of a functionality and simulator (`advantage_replacement_eq_kernelRun` states the kernel replacement gap with it)

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.MPC.composeDistin.why: per-instance concrete composition distinguisher for arbitrary `ProbComp Bool` distinguishers (no security parameter); asymptotic certified composition is tracked in #6045 and #5293

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.MPC.ddhOTReductio.why: tracked in #5293 section 2 (MPC: per-instance DDH-OT reduction with exact uniform exponents; the family-level `ddhOTReceiverToDDHDistinguisher` is certified)

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.MPC.yaoBothEvalua.why: per-instance concrete bound for arbitrary distinguishers (two-output protocol, finite point-and-permute garbling, no security parameter); the asymptotic two-output family with a certified reduction is `Yao.family` (`Scheme.PrvSimSecureUniversal.yaoHybridSemiHonestSecure`, `Yao.isPPT_evaluatorToPrvSim`); a one-sided family is a follow-up recorded on #5293 (https://github.com/cslib-community/cslib-frontier/issues/5293#issuecomment-6908442350)

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.MPC.yaoEvaluatorD.why: per-instance concrete bound for arbitrary distinguishers (one-sided protocol, finite point-and-permute garbling, no security parameter); the asymptotic two-output family with a certified reduction is `Yao.family` (`Scheme.PrvSimSecureUniversal.yaoHybridSemiHonestSecure`, `Yao.isPPT_evaluatorToPrvSim`); a one-sided family is a follow-up recorded on #5293 (https://github.com/cslib-community/cslib-frontier/issues/5293#issuecomment-6908442350)

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SigmaProtocol.Fia.headline: Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.DiscreteLog.eufCma_schnorrNativeROMScheme
Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SigmaProtocol.Fia.why: generic Fiat–Shamir forking reduction; the equality is instance-scoped: it holds only at the word Schnorr protocol `schnorrWordSigma` of a deterministic group description with the sampled simulator `schnorrSampledSimulate`, the word extractor, fallback `0` and the decoded saved-coin forger of a native machine, where for every machine, budget and width with `2 ^ width n` at most the group order, it equates the discrete-log game of the native forking adversary with the one-way game of the reduction; the headline's proof path also passes through `schnorrWordROMSchemeReduction`, the reduction at the perfect word simulator, which stays a gap of its own as a statistical link, so this entry does not cover the whole path; the typed Schnorr bound with `linearSimulate` is an exact bound that applies no assumption

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SigmaProtocol.Imp.headline: Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.negligible_schnorrDirectProbGame
Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SigmaProtocol.Imp.why: generic rewinding extractor of an impersonator; the equality is instance-scoped: it holds only at the typed view `A.typed n (k n)` of a word Schnorr impersonator with the word extractor `wordExtract F (k n)` and the word key generator, where for every setup, challenge length `k`, impersonator and `n`, with no hypotheses, it equates the one-way game of the reduction with the discrete-log game of the word rewinding adversary; the headline applies the assumption to the program through `isPPTOn_rewind` and reaches the reduction only through the exact bound `succProbability_schnorrDirectProbGame_le` and its ideal-key step `succProbability_schnorrDirectGame_le_ideal`, and the eavesdropping headline reaches it through the same step at `A.toDirect k Q`; the Lyubashevsky and typed Schnorr bounds are exact bounds at other instances that apply no assumption

Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SigmaProtocol.Imp.headline: Cslib.Crypto.PrimeOrderGroupFamily.negligible_schnorrEavesdropProbGame
Cslib.Crypto.Protocols.SigmaProtocol.Imp.why: generic simulated-views reduction of an eavesdropper; the equality is instance-scoped: it holds only at the word Schnorr instance, the typed view `A.typed n (k n) (Q n)` of a word Schnorr eavesdropper (statements `⟨d, u⟩` seen as `(d, encode d u)`, word commitments and responses, `k n`-bit challenges, `Q n` conversations read as words) with the sampled simulator `schnorrSampledSimulate n`, the law of the strict-PPT simulator, where for every challenge length `k`, conversation count `Q`, eavesdropper and `n`, with no hypotheses, it equates the typed view `(A.toDirect k Q).typed n (k n)` of the word direct impersonator with the reduction; the headline applies the assumption to the rewinding adversary of the program through `isPPT_toDirect` and `isPPTOn_rewind`, after the separate statistical steps from the native key and honest conversations to the ideal key and simulated conversations (`advantage_schnorrEavesdropProbGame_schnorrDirectGame_le`); the typed Schnorr equality with `linearSimulate` is an exact equality at another instance that applies no assumption
